segments.text: Hello again.
Day ten.
Today is about your nights.
If you've been sleeping well, wonderful.
Stay anyway, because the wind-down we build today is worth having.
And if your nights have been strange, you're far from the only one.
Sleep can be patchy for a while, and dreams can feel very vivid.
Lots of people dream they've used again, and wake up feeling guilty.
That's very common, and it doesn't mean anything has gone wrong.
If that's happened to you, notice the feeling you woke up with.
Relief that it wasn't real.
Maybe even a flash of disappointment in the dream itself.
That tells you something good.
It tells you which side you're on.
A dream isn't a slip.
Nothing is undone.
You get up, and it's still your day.
One thing that often helps.
Smoking makes your body clear caffeine faster.
So after you stop, your usual coffee or tea can hit harder, and keep you awake.
A smaller cup, earlier in the day, can help.
If you take regular medicines, tell your doctor or pharmacist you've stopped smoking.
Some medicines work differently once you stop.
Evenings used to end with nicotine for a lot of people.
So your body may be waiting for a signal that the day is over.
Let's give it a new one.
We'll breathe in gently, and let the breath out take about twice as long.
If focusing on your breath doesn't feel good, or breathing is hard for you, just breathe normally and notice your feet on the floor instead.
Breathe in through your nose, slowly.
And out, long and slow, as if you were fogging a window.
Once more.
In.
And all the way out.
Now let your breath find its own rhythm.
A long, slow breath out helps many people settle.
There's also a longer version in your Stress toolkit, called the four, seven, eight breath.
If the hold in the middle feels like too much, shorten it.
A wind-down is just the same few steps, in the same order, most nights.
Screens down a little earlier.
A shower, or something warm to drink.
A few slow breaths.
Your body learns the pattern, the way it once learned the old one.
In a moment, you'll choose your steps.
Keep it short enough that you'll really do it.
Sleep finds its way back.
Be patient with it.
I'll see you in a couple of days.
